text: Analytics: explain the denominator

name: text
text: PAYBRIDGE  |  DEMO MODE · SYNTHETIC DATA · SIMULATED ACTIONS

name: text
text: Success rate

name: text
text:
Captured ÷ (captured + failed) × 100

Example: 80 captured and 20 failed
80 ÷ 100 × 100 = 80%

Pending/authorized rows are excluded from this terminal-payment denominator.

name: text
text: Money metrics

name: text
text:
Captured GMV = sum of captured amounts

GMV is payment volume, not profit.

Profit needs costs and other accounting inputs.

name: text
text: Always say the time window, status set, and denominator used.

Presenter note: Use the simple 80/20 example and state pending rows are excluded from the success-rate formula in the KPI engine.

name: text
text: Interview explanation you can say naturally

name: text
text: PAYBRIDGE  |  DEMO MODE · SYNTHETIC DATA · SIMULATED ACTIONS

name: text
text: “PayBridge is a payment-operations prototype I built to help teams review payment data and investigate unusual failure patterns. It imports compatible records, stores them in SQL, calculates metrics, and uses an investigation workflow to combine database evidence with relevant procedures. An operator reviews the recommendation and records a decision. Some data and incident narratives are synthetic or illustrative, and the approved action is local; the project does not reroute live payment traffic.”

name: text
text: Keep the business problem first. Then explain data, backend, analytics, investigation, and the safety boundary.

Presenter note: Invite the interviewer to pick one step and then trace it to the file and database record.
Repository references: README.md; backend/app/agent/workflow.py; backend/app/services/ingestion_payments.py
